title: Architect dynamic prefetch coordinator and safe redelivery protocol
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Multiple worker topologies show tail p99 token-latency regressions under bursty traffic. Analysis shows two compounding causes: 1) conservative global prefetch windows cause cold K/V cache misses for recently warmed model shards, and 2) our current redelivery flow (simple reenqueue) creates duplicate inflight windows and spikes head-of-line delays when many messages are requeued simultaneously.

Goal: Design and implement a Dynamic Prefetch Coordinator (DPC) that tracks per-shard recent hit-rate and inflight footprints to recommend adaptive prefetch windows, and a Safe Redelivery Protocol (SRP) that ensures deterministic handoff, idempotency tokens, and rate-aware replay to avoid bursty reenqueue storms. Both pieces should be backward-compatible and feature-flagged for progressive rollout.

Scope and deliverables:
- DPC service: lightweight coordinator that consumes ingress and worker telemetry (hit/miss, seq lengths, inflight counts) and emits per-shard prefetch targets. Expose a gRPC endpoint for workers to query suggestions and an HTTP debug dashboard with small heatmap.
- Local worker changes: add a non-blocking prefetch adaptor that implements DPC suggestions with soft limits and exponential decay when under memory pressure. Add metric hooks for misses by cause.
- SRP flow: on redelivery, attach an idempotency token (UUID + originating-offset) and write a short-lived acknowledgement key in Redis to prevent duplicate processing across retries. Implement rate-aware redelivery queue with token-bucket smoothing aggregated by tenant to spread replays. Provide a fallthrough that preserves original semantics if SRP is disabled.
- Tests: stress harness on staging with synthetic burst patterns, p99 latency dashboards, correctness tests for idempotency, and chaos tests for coordinator flapping.

Tradeoffs considered:
- Centralized coordinator vs fully local heuristics: coordinator slightly increases control-plane complexity but enables cross-worker harmonization and faster adaptation to global load changes.
- Redis ack keys for idempotency vs sticky-offset logs: Redis was chosen for low-latency checks and TTL semantics; will add instrumentation to measure Redis RPS impact.
- Rate-aware redelivery increases latency for some retries to avoid system-wide head-of-line blocking — acceptable as it reduces customer-visible p99 spikes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Under synthetic burst tests, tail token-latency p99 reduces by >= 25% vs baseline and mean latency does not regress > 5%.
- No duplicate side-effects observed in correctness tests for 100k redeliveries in harness.
- DPC and SRP behind flags with runtime configs; rollout plan documented.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flags, limited to internal canary tenants. 2) Enable DPC read-only mode (suggestions only) and validate metrics for 48h. 3) Enable worker-enforced prefetch on 10% tenants, monitor. 4) Enable SRP redelivery smoothing for non-production tenants, validate idempotency. 5) Gradually increase to all tenants with rollback playbook.

Monitoring and dashboards:
- New dashboard: prefetch_hit_rate by shard, SRP_replay_rate, redis_ack_hit_ratio, p99_token_latency_by_tenant.
- Alerting: prefetch_hit_rate drop > 30% sustained for 5m, redis_ack_key_error_rate > 1%.
